narrative.title: Runner-Up Power Draw
narrative.scenario: A datacenter ranks rack power draw to plan failover capacity. The top rack is already handled by a dedicated circuit, so the facility team needs the second highest distinct draw across the fleet. If every rack draws the same power there is no runner-up, and the answer is -1.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n followed by an array Arr of n integer power draws.
narrative.outputFormat: The second largest distinct value in Arr, or -1 when no such value exists.

testCases.explanation: 35 is the largest distinct draw and 34 is the next one down, so the runner-up is 34.
The draws climb monotonically, so the runner-up keeps shifting forward as 10 passes it.

hintLevels: Level 1: Track two positions at once - the champion so far and the best value that is strictly below the champion.
Level 2: Walk left to right; when a reading beats the champion, the old champion becomes the runner-up, otherwise compare the reading against the runner-up instead.
Level 3: The word distinct matters. Repeated copies of the maximum must never be promoted to runner-up, and an all-equal buffer has no runner-up at all.
